reason: [Security][jvm] kof4shell (CVE-2026-114938): the HotSpot AVX-512 Base64 decode intrinsic (Intel Ice Lake+/AMD Zen 4+, JDK 17.0.6+/21/25) overflows the heap on padded inputs — unauthenticated RCE. Kof exposure measured: 87 java.util.Base64 sites in the generated JVM runtime (crypto/web/tls/acme/config) + the CLI itself. MITIGATED same cycle: -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics ships by DEFAULT on every JVM Kof launches (bin/kof(+.bat), the KofStdio flag helpers, the JS-driver re-exec, the debug session); KOF_B64_INTRINSICS=1 opts out for a fixed JDK (11.0.33.1/17.0.21.1/21.0.13.1/25.0.5.1/27.0.1.1). The issue tracks the default flipping back: embedded JDK >= a fixed build, proven on AVX-512 hardware.
owner: security lane; the embedded-JDK bump = the release front

reason: [Gap][stdlib] no terminal module — an interactive TUI today has to hand-write libc FFI (`isatty`/`tcgetattr`/`cfmakeraw`/`tcsetattr`/`read`/`write`/`ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)`) plus `buffer.peek8`/`poke8` to serialize the 60-byte `struct termios`, because `Buffer(U8)` is not a user type. The FFI path IS reachable and was measured by the reporter in a pty (40x120, identical on JVM and the Native x86-64 binary). A new stdlib surface (`kof.term` proposed) is OUTSIDE the 1.0 surface, not a correction: no 1.0 program is left without a path, and the proposal admits honest degradation where there is no TTY. Correction recorded on the issue: the claim that FFI is "the ONLY path to a terminal program joining JVM and Native" holds only when the same source must run on both — on the JVM alone `kof.process` already solves `stty`/`tput` without `foreign module`. Closure criterion = an opaque termios handle, a typed `readKey` decoding `ESC[A`, and honest degradation with its own code, proven on the three targets with no `foreign module` in user source.

reason: [Bug][jvm] encoding.base64Encode/hexEncode accept Int and Int[] with no diagnostic and emit invalid bytecode — measured on tip 663669344: `kof check` says "no errors" for `encoding.base64Encode(123)`, `javap` shows `invokestatic kof_encoding_base64Encode:(Ljava/lang/String;)` with an int on the stack, the JVM refuses the class (VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack), JS silently returns "" (the utf8 loop over a number never runs) and the Native binary SIGSEGVs. Root cause: `KofEncoding.staticMethod` gates on ARGUMENT COUNT only (`argc == 1`) and never on the type; the same anti-pattern the ledger already records for `math.*` in §658. `1.0-blocks` because one source is admitted by every target and behaves in three different ways. Fix = type guard (SEM025 naming the face) PLUS the additive `Int[]` overload the reporting TUI actually needs (`File.readBytes()` already returns `Int[]`).

reason: [Gap] kof.http has no byte face — `JvmHttpResponseRuntime.jvmSource` uses `BodyHandlers.ofString()` for the response and `BodyPublishers.ofString(body)` for the request, and the `kof.http.Response` handle carries only a `String` body. A non-UTF8 download (e.g. a PNG starting with 0x89) is decoded with replacement characters and is IRRECOVERABLE; measured on tip 663669344 with a local 250-byte PNG: `resposta.status()`=200, `resposta.body().length`=81 (plausible) and `encoding.hexEncode(body.substring(0,8))`=`efbfbd504e470d0a1a0a` instead of `89504e470d0a1a0a` — silent data corruption reported as success, no diagnostic code. `1.0-blocks`: a 1.0 program that downloads media silently corrupts it and has no way to notice; `D-1.0-BLOCKS-NO-HONEST-LIMITS` requires an honest code where a limit exists — here there is neither a limit nor a code. Fix = raw-bytes face on the response (`Int[]`) + `getBytes`/`sendBytes`, additive, `body()` untouched; RED-first test with a local server serving non-UTF8 bytes.
owner: measured + classified by triage lane 192.168.15.30:9093 21/11 (repro corrected on the issue: `http.responseStatus`/`http.responseBody` do not exist — from #1126 the acessors are instance methods on `http.send`'s Response)

reason: [Bug][jvm] an INCREMENTAL `kof build --target jvm --fat` reuses the generated `KofRuntime.class` from the previous build, so a record added since then has NO `kof_json_decode_<pkg>_<Record>` helper and the jar dies at run with NoSuchMethodError; `rm -rf build` fixes it. ROOT CAUSE measured on tip 624bf2bba: `JvmRuntime.ensureCompiled` (kof-compiler/src/main/java/dev/kof/compiler/jvm/JvmRuntime.java:102-105) does `if (Files.exists(runtimeDir.resolve("KofRuntime.class"))) return;` — the generated source embeds the per-record JSON decoders from the module's class list and is never regenerated when the runtime class already exists. Proved with the issue's exact project: clean build runs `alfa=1`; incremental build after adding `record Beta` prints `NoSuchMethodError kof_json_decode_app_Beta` and the embedded runtime carries ONLY `kof_json_decode_app_Alfa`; `rm -rf build` + rebuild carries both and prints `alfa=1 beta=2`. CLASSIFIED 1.0-blocks per D-1.0-BLOCKS-NO-HONEST-LIMITS (the build says ok and the artifact is broken — a no-silent-fallback violation): the criterion = an incremental rebuild of the same tree produces a jar that runs, or the build fails when the emitted bytecode calls a runtime helper the packaged runtime lacks — with a RED-first test.
owner: reported by the probe lane (issue #1187); root cause measured + classified by lane issues/triage 192.168.15.30:9093 22/11

reason: [Bug][jvm] a JDK generic method typed `Object` (e.g. `HttpResponse.body()`) passed where a `String` is expected PASSES `kof check` and emits invalid bytecode (invokeinterface ...()Ljava/lang/Object; into an <init>(I Ljava/lang/String;)V), so the class fails to load with VerifyError (masked as the false 'JavaFX runtime not found' message when launched from a fat jar). ROOT CAUSE measured on tip 624bf2bba, reduced WITHOUT java.net.http: `TypeChecker.emitCtorPairCompatible` (kof-compiler/src/main/java/dev/kof/compiler/TypeChecker.java:102-110) ends with `if (formal instanceof Type.ClassType && arg instanceof Type.ClassType) return true;` — class-vs-class is accepted with no hierarchy check, so a record constructor `Caixa(String)` accepts `Object`. The SAME assignment on a local is correctly refused (`var s: String = o` -> SEM021), so the blind spot is the CONSTRUCTOR path only. Proved with `record Caixa(String s)` + `var o: Object = 42` + `Caixa(o)`: check 'no errors', load VerifyError 'Object is not assignable to String'. CLASSIFIED 1.0-blocks per D-1.0-BLOCKS-NO-HONEST-LIMITS (a real JVM codegen bug in a supported 1.0 face IS a tracked 1.0 edge): the criterion = the constructor path uses the same class-hierarchy rule as the local assignment (SEM014/SEM021), keeping the permissive arm only for EXTERNAL classes — with a RED-first test.
owner: reported by the probe lane (issue #1188); root cause measured + classified by lane issues/triage 192.168.15.30:9093 22/11

reason: [Bug][jvm] an EXISTING String method called with the WRONG ARITY (`"abcdef".substring(1, 3, 4)`) passes `kof check` and the build emits `java/lang/String.substring:(III)` -> NoSuchMethodError at run. ROOT CAUSE measured on tip 624bf2bba: the arity table `StringMethodRegistry.stringMethodSignature` DOES return null for the wrong arity, but it is consulted only for the RETURN TYPE (`BuiltinCallTailTyper` ~239-250 falls to `default -> UNKNOWN` with no diagnostic) and the emit keeps the args and fabricates the descriptor; the by-position argument guards in `StringReceiverGuards` (SEM051/SEM014) never run for a method whose signature is null, and `StringUnknownMethodGuard` only covers unknown NAMES, not wrong arity. Reducible face: the same call feeding a consumer keeps the program green while a UNKNOWN type flows on (e.g. `a.length()` emitted on an UNKNOWN receiver). The guard runs in the SHARED frontend (`ExpressionInstanceCallLowerer:326`), so the fix covers JVM/Native/JS/WASI/Script. CLASSIFIED 1.0-blocks per D-1.0-BLOCKS-NO-HONEST-LIMITS (compiles, says 'no errors', dies at run — no-silent-fallback violation): the criterion = a compile-time diagnostic naming the valid signatures, mirroring the `indexOf` SEM051 message — with a RED-first test. | FIXED 22/11 (lane issues/triage 192.168.15.30:9093): StringReceiverGuards.checkArity rejects a registry verb whose arity no overload takes with SEM014 naming the valid arities; Tri9093StringArityE2ETest 3/0F (RED-first, both the direct call and the UNKNOWN-leak face); String family 173-run regression with only environmental/unrelated reds.
